answer.evidence: This is a flat, front-facing sign panel. The brown board (rows 6-28) with its white lettering is a vertical face. The light cap at rows 1-4 has a pink label inside it, so it reads as a frame header facing the viewer, not a horizontal surface. The gray-blue line at row 4 (#738a90) is mirrored by the bottom frame strip at rows 29-30 (#738a90/#61767d), which makes it frame trim. The only top-like part is a 1-2 row rim. No ellipse, no roof plane and no contents are visible, and no side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin vertical sign: a brown board with a lighter frame edge, darker side shading, and white Korean lettering. It has 9 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 7%, close to bus-shelter-a (9%) and far from a large flat fill. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans dark brown and follows the material rather than a black sticker line. The brown face shows only about 3-4 steps, fewer than the richer references, and the panel is fairly plain apart from the lettering. For a thin single-purpose sign, it would sit acceptably next to bus-shelter-a without looking thinner or more sticker-like.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical brown signboard with a lighter edge, white Hangul lettering and a dark brown outline. Measured against the modern_city references, its 9 visible tones per tile sit above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 7%, slightly better than bus-shelter-a (9%) and within the range of the other references. The dark edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, so the outline is tinted dark brown, matching the board material rather than a sticker-style black line. By eye, the board face has a lit edge, a mid tone and a dark side, plus the lettering, so about 4 steps against roughly 5 on the references. It is a simple prop, and a plain sign board is not penalised for lacking the vending machine's detail.
